:::{#exm-cond-pmf}

#### Conditional PMF from a vaccine trial

The `vaccine` dataset in the `dobson` package
(@dobson4e, Table 9.6)
records the responses in a flu vaccine trial:
$X$ is treatment group (placebo or vaccine)
and $Y$ is the level of response to treatment (small, moderate, or large).

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
response_levels <- c("small", "moderate", "large")
vaccine_tab <-
  dobson::vaccine |>
  dplyr::mutate(response = factor(response, levels = response_levels)) |>
  xtabs(frequency ~ treatment + response, data = _)
pander::pander(as.data.frame.matrix(vaccine_tab))
n_vaccine <- sum(vaccine_tab)
n_placebo <- vaccine_tab["placebo", ]
```

Choose one of the $n = `r n_vaccine`$ trial participants at random
(a [random choice](probability-basics.qmd#def-random-choice)),
and let $(X, Y)$ be that participant's treatment and response.
The [joint PMF](random-variables.qmd#def-joint-pmf) of $(X, Y)$ is then the table of frequencies divided by the total
$n$ trial participants.
By the [marginal PMF theorem](random-variables.qmd#thm-marginal-pmf),
the [marginal](random-variables.qmd#def-marginal) probability $\P(X = \text{placebo})$ is:

$$
\ba
\P(X = \text{placebo})
&= \P(X = \text{placebo},\, Y = \text{small})
 + \P(X = \text{placebo},\, Y = \text{moderate})
 + \P(X = \text{placebo},\, Y = \text{large})
&& \text{(marginal PMF from the joint PMF)}
\\&= \tfrac{`r n_placebo[["small"]]`}{`r n_vaccine`}
 + \tfrac{`r n_placebo[["moderate"]]`}{`r n_vaccine`}
 + \tfrac{`r n_placebo[["large"]]`}{`r n_vaccine`}
&& \text{(read the table)}
\\&= \tfrac{`r sum(n_placebo)`}{`r n_vaccine`}
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$

By @def-cond-pmf, the conditional PMF of $Y$ given $X = \text{placebo}$ is:

$$
\ba
\P(Y = \text{small} \mid X = \text{placebo})
&= \frac{\P(X = \text{placebo},\, Y = \text{small})}{\P(X = \text{placebo})}
&& \text{(definition of conditional PMF)}
\\&= \frac{`r n_placebo[["small"]]`/`r n_vaccine`}{`r sum(n_placebo)`/`r n_vaccine`}
&& \text{(substitute)}
\\&= \frac{`r n_placebo[["small"]]`}{`r sum(n_placebo)`}
&& \text{(cancel } `r n_vaccine` \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::
